migration_notes.message: M52 adds typed contract/page/error metadata while preserving legacy response keys for existing dashboard consumers.

execution_backends.label: Desktop node
execution_backends.description: Hand work off to a paired first-party desktop node when a healthy node is available.
tradeoffs: Supports first-party desktop capabilities and local mediation flows
Depends on node heartbeat, pairing trust, and explicit rollout opt-in

execution_backends.label: Docker
execution_backends.description: Run work inside an explicit container profile with workspace changes returning as a reviewed patch bundle.
tradeoffs: Requires an allowlisted image and non-privileged container profile
Authoritative workspace writes return as patch bundles for review

execution_backends.label: Local sandbox
execution_backends.description: Run work on the daemon host and keep sandbox/process-runner guardrails local.
tradeoffs: Cannot satisfy first-party desktop-native capability requests by itself

execution_backends.label: Networked worker
execution_backends.description: Run work on an attested ephemeral worker with proxy-mediated egress and scoped artifact transport.
tradeoffs: Requires explicit worker attestation plus cleanup verification before use
Worker leases stay ephemeral with ttl<=900000ms and fail closed on cleanup gaps

execution_backends.label: SSH tunnel
execution_backends.description: Use an operator-established SSH tunnel for remote control-plane access and remote operator workflows.
tradeoffs: Useful for explicit remote operator access and controlled handoff
Requires manual tunnel setup and does not replace sandbox or node trust boundaries

rollout maturity states, owners, required tests, public exposure, and promotion blockers
public method descriptors, route scopes, schema hashes, streaming flags, and idempotency support
registered OpenAI-compatible route surface probed by the live daemon harness
top-level CLI families and parity status used by operator handoff surfaces
local, desktop, Docker, networked worker, and SSH backend posture

MCP serve is discoverable, while external MCP import/supervision remains roadmap work
delegated work surfaces exist behind preview controls before durable subagent records land
local sandbox is available, while remote backends and workers remain gated or disabled
regression fixtures exist before the dedicated QA Lab manifest and runner
basic hook operability is exposed before the full agent hook taxonomy
diagnostics and metrics sections are emitted by the live daemon harness
recovery flags are visible but default-off before classifier and stream-normalizer work
